logical_contracts.name: source-authority
logical_contracts.invariant: Current user local files/logs outrank workspace, release, and historical anchors.

logical_contracts.name: browser-server-authority
logical_contracts.invariant: Browser is presentation; credentials, routing, persistence, and security policy remain server authoritative.

logical_contracts.name: canonical-representation
logical_contracts.invariant: Build-time page.md is canonical; browser conversion is convenience.

logical_contracts.name: turn-owned-cancellation
logical_contracts.invariant: Stopped or superseded turns cannot append late work, retry reasoning, create previews, or unlock newer UI.

logical_contracts.name: latest-file-authority
logical_contracts.invariant: Every generated-file link resolves the newest state; broken/unavailable newer revisions never reveal stale bytes.

logical_contracts.name: conversation-generation-binding
logical_contracts.invariant: Async share/contribution results must remain bound to the conversation generation that initiated them.

logical_contracts.name: telemetry-consent
logical_contracts.invariant: Local feedback works without network telemetry; network telemetry/contribution remains explicit-consent gated.

logical_contracts.name: hermetic-release-subprocesses
logical_contracts.invariant: Release-security subprocesses use constrained environments and do not inherit arbitrary secrets or Git authority.

logical_contracts.name: maintenance-separation
logical_contracts.invariant: Runtime never imports maintenance/skill planes; planning, history, dev-only tools, and backups stay outside runtime.

logical_contracts.name: test-first-repair
logical_contracts.invariant: Local failures are classified and fixed narrowly before broad reruns or new feature work.
